# Rig setup checklist

Every reading here is recorded by `tools/pilot.py setup`, and the cut gate refuses to open
until all of them exist and pass. They are properties of the rig, not of the garment: freeze
them once and every capture in the session carries the hash of this configuration.

## The frozen configuration

- [ ] Camera model recorded
- [ ] Mount height above the surface measured and recorded (cm)
- [ ] Lens chosen for whole-garment frames and locked
- [ ] Backdrop identified, and it will not change during the session
- [ ] Lighting model and setting recorded
- [ ] The frozen gap between the legs decided and recorded (cm)
- [ ] Exposure and white balance locked
- [ ] Room recorded

## The calibration readings

- [ ] **empty_backdrop** — a frame of the backdrop with nothing on it, so a mark on the cloth can later be told from a mark on the garment
- [ ] **board_verification** — the board photographed and detected, so the detector is known to work on this print under this light
- [ ] **board_square_measured** — a run of squares measured with a steel rule. The board declares 25.0 mm; a printer that scaled to 95% puts that error into every measurement in the study
- [ ] **lighting_test** — no hotspot or shadow across the area the garment will occupy
- [ ] **exposure_white_balance** — a grey or white card photographed with the locked settings, so colour change through washing has a reference
- [ ] **camera_height** — measured and recorded, because it sets the scale and the depth of field
- [ ] **lens_selection** — chosen and locked; changing lens mid-session changes the geometry
- [ ] **backdrop_identified** — named, so a change of backdrop is a recorded deviation
- [ ] **daylight_controlled** — daylight excluded or constant. A session that starts at noon and ends at dusk has two colour temperatures in it
- [ ] **board_garment_coplanar** — a low-angle frame showing the board and the garment on one surface. If the board sits on a book, every scale is wrong by the thickness of the book

The board's squares must measure 25.0 mm within 0.5 mm. Measure a run of eight and divide: a
single square is too short to read to that precision.
